title: Hurricane ‘Polo’: Mexican Navy Deploys Nearly 3,000 Personnel in Support of Baja California Sur
author: Iván Evair Saldaña and César Arellano
content:
_This article by[Iván Evair Saldaña and César
Arellano](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Iv%C3%A1n%20Evair%20Salda%C3%B1a%20y%20C%C3%A9sar%20Arellano)
originally appeared in the [September 27, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/27/estados/huracan-polo-
marina-despliega-casi-3-mil-elementos-en-apoyo-a-bcs), Mexico's premier left
wing daily newspaper._

The Secretariat of the Navy-Mexican Navy reported this Sunday that it keeps
**2,923 personnel deployed in Baja California Sur** , in addition to vehicles,
aircraft and specialized equipment, to assist the population affected by
Hurricane _Polo_ , which as of the early hours of the day remained a Category
3.

As part of the reinforcement of the Plan Marina, at 08:30 the ship Isla
Tiburón set sail for Mazatlán, Sinaloa, with an MI-17 helicopter, 2,000 food
packages, 8,000 liters of drinking water, two backhoes, three Ural vehicles,
three Zodiac boats and sapper equipment.

![Navy ship with an MI-17 helicopter on deck and a Plan Marina
banner](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/02-isla-
tiburon.jpg)Photo: Semar

Of the personnel deployed in Baja California Sur, 589 were concentrated in the
Naval Sector of Santa Rosalía, in anticipation of greater damage in that area.
The Navy indicated that _Polo_ **could make landfall on Monday as a Category 2
hurricane** , after gradually weakening in the coming hours.

In addition, in coordination with authorities from the three levels of
government, **111 temporary shelters were set up** in La Paz, Los Cabos,
Comondú, Loreto and Mulegé, with a combined capacity to house 14,445 people.

As a preventive measure, the maritime authority closed the port of San Blas,
Nayarit, to all types of vessels, while Cabo San Lucas, San José del Cabo, San
Carlos, Bahía Magdalena and Loreto, in Baja California Sur, as well as Barra
de Navidad, Jalisco, remain closed to small vessels.

![Navy personnel with shovels and picks in front of a Plan Marina
vehicle](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/03-marines-
plan-marina.jpg)Photo: Semar
